title: Strategic airline alliances: governance, selective integration, and networks of networks
book_title: Research Handbook on Air Transport Leadership and Governance
author_source: Albers, van den Oord, Koch and Mandt, in Research Handbook on Air Transport Leadership and Governance, Edward Elgar, 2025, handbook chapter 20
note: Chapter 20 of the Elgar research handbook on strategic airline alliances (Star Alliance, oneworld, SkyTeam): alliance governance structures, 'selective integration' of members into activities such as code-sharing, joint procurement and metal-neutral joint ventures, and the resulting 'networks of networks' in which bilateral and multilateral JVs nest within the global alliances.
relevance: Theory and context: the single closest match to the research question; it explicitly conceptualises selective (differentiated) integration of alliance members and nested JV tiers in the airline industry. Editors of the handbook not captured; check on Elgaronline. Access: paid, handbook approx. GBP 200; chapter PDF via Elgaronline (WU licence if subscribed).

title: Strategic Alliance Management
author_source: Tjemkes, Vos and Burgers, Routledge, 2023 (3rd ed.), textbook
note: Textbook structured along the alliance life cycle (strategy, partner selection, negotiation, design, launch, management, evaluation, termination) with dedicated chapters on alliance governance and control, multipartner alliances, alliance portfolios, alliance networks, international alliances, and alliance capability; third edition adds ecosystems and digital platforms.
relevance: Theory and teaching context: up-to-date synthesis with separate chapters on multipartner alliances, portfolios and international alliances, i.e. the three loci of differentiated integration; useful for construct definitions. Access: paperback approx. GBP 50; Taylor & Francis e-book via WU licence if subscribed.

title: Integration and Differentiation in the European Union: Theory and Policies
outlet: Palgrave Macmillan (European Union Politics series), 2nd edition
author_source: Leuffen, Rittberger and Schimmelfennig, Palgrave Macmillan, 2022 (2nd ed.), monograph
note: The standard textbook on differentiated integration (DI). Defines integration along three dimensions (level of centralisation, functional scope, territorial extension) and differentiation as variation in membership and depth across policy areas; compares intergovernmentalist, supranationalist and constructivist explanations and applies them to the single market, EMU, Schengen, security and enlargement.
relevance: Theory: the conceptual source for transferring 'level, scope and extension' of integration to alliances (which activities, which partners, how deep). Gives the typology (multi-speed, variable geometry, a la carte, vertical vs horizontal differentiation) and testable hypotheses (interdependence, politicisation, heterogeneity). Access: paid, hardback approx. EUR 60, paperback approx. EUR 40; e-book via WU licence if Springer EU politics collection is subscribed.

title: The Routledge Handbook of Differentiation in the European Union
author_source: Leruth, Gänzle and Trondal (eds.), Routledge, 2022, handbook (c. 45 chapters)
note: The most comprehensive reference work on differentiation in the EU: conceptual and theoretical chapters (intergovernmentalism, neofunctionalism, postfunctionalism, federalism, public-goods theory), methods and measurement chapters, policy-area chapters (EMU, Schengen, defence, single market), external differentiation and legitimacy. Several chapters are open access via OAPEN.
relevance: Theory and method: one-stop source for DI theories and the measurement chapters that an IB paper can borrow for coding alliance differentiation; the public-goods (club goods) chapters connect to alliance economics. Access: hardback approx. GBP 190, paperback approx. GBP 50; some chapters open access on library.oapen.org.

title: Ever Looser Union? Differentiated European Integration
author_source: Schimmelfennig and Winzen, Oxford University Press, 2020, monograph
note: Quantitative study of differentiated integration as a legal instrument: a dataset of all treaty- and legislation-based differentiations since the 1950s shows that DI is used to overcome deadlock, distinguishes instrumental (temporary, capacity-driven) from constitutional (lasting, sovereignty-driven) differentiation, and tests demand- and supply-side explanations.
relevance: Method and theory: the only book-length quantitative measurement of differentiation (counts of opt-outs/exemptions by member, policy and time) and a template for building a 'differentiation index' for alliance members (e.g. activities an airline opts into or out of within an alliance). Access: paid, hardback approx. GBP 70; Oxford Scholarship Online via WU licence if subscribed.

title: Differentiated Integration and Disintegration in a Post-Brexit Era
author_source: Gänzle, Leruth and Trondal (eds.), Routledge, 2020, edited volume
note: Twelve chapters on differentiation, differentiated integration and differentiated disintegration after Brexit: conceptual chapter by the editors, chapters on exit and opt-outs, external differentiation (EEA, Switzerland), administrative differentiation and legitimacy. Introduces 'differentiated disintegration' as the mirror image of DI.
relevance: Theory and gap: supplies the exit/partial-exit vocabulary (differentiated disintegration) useful for alliance member withdrawals, downgrades to lower tiers, or carve-outs of activities from a JV. Access: paid, hardback approx. GBP 130, paperback approx. GBP 40; Taylor & Francis e-book via WU licence if subscribed.

title: Cooperative Strategy: Managing Alliances and Networks
author_source: Child, Faulkner, Tallman and Hsieh, Oxford University Press, 2019 (3rd ed.), textbook/monograph
note: Comprehensive treatment of cooperative strategy: motives and theories (TCE, RBV, game theory, trust), alliance forms (JVs, collaborations, consortia, networks, multi-partner alliances), partner selection, control and governance, learning, culture, evolution and termination, with chapters on networks and international alliances. The 2019 edition adds platforms and ecosystems. (Note: 3rd, not 2nd, edition.)
relevance: Theory and context: the chapters on control and governance of IJVs and on multi-partner alliances/constellations frame how deep each partner integrates; good source for defining degrees of integration (contractual to equity to merger). Access: paid, hardback approx. GBP 95, paperback approx. GBP 50; Oxford e-book may be in WU licence.

title: Managing Alliance Portfolios and Networks
outlet: Information Age Publishing (Research in Strategic Alliances series)
author_source: Das (ed.), Information Age Publishing, 2017, edited volume (9 chapters)
note: Nine chapters on alliance portfolios and networks: portfolio perspective on alliance constellations, alliance management capability, competition dynamics of alliance networks, value creation in alliance ecosystems, internationalisation of an SME's alliance portfolio, structural embeddedness during industry convergence.
relevance: Theory: portfolio configuration (partner, functional and governance diversity) is the firm-level counterpart of differentiated integration; the internationalisation chapter links portfolios to cross-border scope. Access: paperback approx. USD 50; chapters on Emerald Insight (WU licence if subscribed).

title: Managing Multipartner Strategic Alliances
outlet: Information Age Publishing (Research in Strategic Alliances series)
author_source: Das (ed.), Information Age Publishing, 2015, edited volume (10 chapters)
note: Ten chapters on alliances with more than two members: formation choice, complexity and coordination, power and roles of members, governance of multipartner alliances, value creation and appropriation, and performance; includes conceptual and empirical work (e.g. 'The choice and formation of multipartner alliances: underpinning factors').
relevance: Theory and gap: multipartner alliances (airline groupings, R&D consortia) are where differentiated integration is most visible, yet the volume shows that member heterogeneity in integration depth is rarely modelled explicitly. Access: paperback approx. USD 50, hardback approx. USD 95.

title: Which Europe? The Politics of Differentiated Integration
outlet: Palgrave Macmillan (Palgrave Studies in European Union Politics)
author_source: Dyson and Sepos (eds.), Palgrave Macmillan, 2010, edited volume
note: Edited volume that first systematised the forms of differentiated integration (multi-speed, variable geometry, a la carte, concentric circles, core Europe) and traced them across policy fields (EMU, Schengen, defence, enlargement) and member-state 'pioneers' and 'laggards'; the introduction by Dyson and Sepos offers a typology by time, space and matter.
relevance: Theory/context: the time-space-matter typology maps directly onto alliance questions (differentiation over time = phased integration; over space = regional sub-alliances; over matter = selective functional integration). Access: paid, hardback approx. GBP 100; chapters on SpringerLink via WU licence if subscribed. Link is the SpringerLink book page constructed from the e-ISBN and has not been checked.

title: Strategic Alliances
book_title: The Oxford Handbook of International Business (2nd edition)
author_source: Inkpen, in Rugman (ed.), Oxford Handbook of International Business, OUP, 2009, handbook chapter
note: Handbook chapter reviewing international strategic alliance research: definitions and forms (equity JVs vs non-equity), rationales (TCE, RBV, learning), alliance governance and control, performance measurement, instability and the alliance-learning debate; identifies open research questions.
relevance: Theory: authoritative IB review that positions control and governance as the main lever for 'how much' to integrate with a partner; good for the literature review framing. Access: paperback approx. GBP 40; Oxford Handbooks Online via WU licence if subscribed. Page range beyond the start page (389) not confirmed.

title: Alliances and Joint Ventures: The Role of Partner Selection from an Embeddedness Perspective
book_title: The Oxford Handbook of Inter-Organizational Relations
author_source: Dacin, Reid and Ring, in Cropper, Ebers, Huxham and Ring (eds.), Oxford Handbook of Inter-Organizational Relations, OUP, 2008, handbook chapter
note: Chapter on alliances and JVs in the 808-page handbook of inter-organisational relations: reviews alliance and JV research with a focus on partner selection and embeddedness (relational, structural, institutional), and how prior ties shape governance choice and depth of cooperation.
relevance: Theory: embeddedness explains why some partners within the same alliance are integrated more deeply (prior ties, trust) than others, an explanation for differentiated integration across partners. Access: handbook paperback approx. GBP 45; Oxford Handbooks Online via WU licence if subscribed.

title: Handbook of Strategic Alliances
author_source: Shenkar and Reuer (eds.), Sage, 2006, handbook
note: Handbook with chapters on theoretical foundations (Casson and Mol on entrepreneurship; Gomes-Casseres 'How alliances reshape competition'; Luo on opportunism; Kale and Zollo on evolutionary theory; real options; alliance networks), alliance management ('Structuring and restructuring alliances', 'Alliance contractual design', 'Interorganizational trust'), research methods, and 'Alliances and international business theory'.
relevance: Theory and method: chapters on structuring/restructuring, contractual design and networks give the governance vocabulary for differentiated integration; the methods chapter is useful for a quantitative design. Access: paid, approx. USD 150; Sage Knowledge e-book under WU licence if subscribed.

title: Global Strategy: Creating and Sustaining Advantage across Borders
author_source: Inkpen and Ramaswamy, Oxford University Press, 2005, monograph
note: Global strategy text with chapters on globalisation and global strategy, entry modes, global alliances and acquisitions, knowledge transfer and learning in alliances, and managing the multinational network; discusses JVs and alliances as vehicles for selective integration of activities across borders.
relevance: Context and theory: the alliance and knowledge-transfer chapters frame why MNEs integrate some value-chain activities with partners and keep others in-house; useful for defining 'activities' as the unit of differentiation. Access: paid, approx. GBP 40; Oxford Scholarship Online via WU licence if subscribed.

title: Strategic Alliances: Theory and Evidence
author_source: Reuer (ed.), Oxford University Press, 2004, edited reader
note: Reader collecting key alliance articles grouped into alliance formation and governance (TCE, real options), alliance dynamics (instability, learning races), and performance; includes Hennart on equity JVs, Kogut on JV instability, Gulati on social structure and governance, and Reuer's own work on IJV restructuring.
relevance: Theory: compact entry point to governance-choice and alliance-evolution literatures that underpin why integration depth is renegotiated over time. Access: paperback approx. GBP 40; Oxford Academic e-book under WU licence if subscribed.

title: Managing Strategic Airline Alliances
outlet: Ashgate (Ashgate Studies in Aviation Economics and Management), now Routledge
author_source: Kleymann and Seristö, Ashgate, 2004, monograph
note: Monograph on the management of global airline alliances: motives, evolution from bilateral code-shares to multilateral groupings, alliance governance and the problem of member heterogeneity, levels of commitment (membership tiers, equity stakes, joint ventures), and the tension between alliance-level integration and member autonomy.
relevance: Context and theory: documents how airline alliances institutionalise differentiated membership (full members, affiliates, JV partners) and the governance problems this creates; pre-dates metal-neutral JVs but frames the integration dilemma. Access: paperback approx. GBP 45; Routledge e-book via WU licence if subscribed.

title: Cooperative Strategies and Alliances
outlet: Pergamon / Elsevier (International Business and Management series)
author_source: Contractor and Lorange (eds.), Pergamon, 2002, edited volume (36 papers)
note: Successor to the 1988 Lexington volume: 36 papers from an IMD conference covering alliance theory (TCE, real options, learning), governance and control, IJV instability and performance, alliance networks and portfolios, and sector studies; includes the editors' chapter 'The growth of alliances in the knowledge-based economy'.
relevance: Theory and gap: a broad map of alliance research streams in which 'how much to integrate' appears as governance choice; useful for positioning differentiated integration as an under-theorised structural feature. Access: paid, approx. GBP 150 new; chapters not individually digitised.

title: Alliance Advantage: The Art of Creating Value through Partnering
author_source: Doz and Hamel, Harvard Business School Press, 1998, monograph
note: Classic practitioner-academic book on alliance value creation: co-option, co-specialisation and learning as alliance logics; design of scope, governance and interface; management of multi-partner 'alliance networks' and alliance evolution; evidence from cases such as airline, telecom and automotive alliances.
relevance: Theory: the co-specialisation and 'scope of cooperation' arguments explain why partners integrate selectively (only where complementary) and why integration depth varies across activities; cited 5,000+ times. Access: out of print in hardback, used copies approx. EUR 15-30; Google Books link constructed from ISBN and not checked.

title: Cooperative Strategies (3 vols.: North American Perspectives; European Perspectives; Asian Pacific Perspectives)
outlet: The New Lexington Press, San Francisco
author_source: Beamish and Killing (eds.), New Lexington Press, 1997, three-volume edited series
note: Three regional volumes from the 1996 Cooperative Strategies conferences: empirical and conceptual chapters on IJV control and performance, learning, trust, partner selection, alliance networks and cross-regional comparisons (North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific).
relevance: Context and theory: the regional structure itself illustrates differentiated integration across regions; several chapters examine split, dominant and shared control in IJVs. Access: out of print, library copies; used sets approx. EUR 50-100.

title: The Alliance Revolution: The New Shape of Business Rivalry
author_source: Gomes-Casseres, Harvard University Press, 1996, monograph
note: Introduces 'constellations' (groups of allied firms competing against other groups) using RISC computing and PDA alliances; analyses how constellations are structured, how members' roles and depth of involvement differ (core vs peripheral members), and how group-based competition changes rivalry.
relevance: Theory: the constellation concept is the closest alliance analogue to variable geometry, with core/periphery tiers and different depths of commitment; foundation for multi-partner and airline-alliance research. Access: paperback approx. USD 35; WU library likely holds.

title: Strategic Alliances: An Entrepreneurial Approach to Globalization
author_source: Yoshino and Rangan, Harvard Business School Press, 1995, monograph
note: Defines strategic alliances (independent firms, shared control, continuing contributions) and proposes a typology by conflict potential and extent of interaction (pro-competitive, non-competitive, competitive, pre-competitive); discusses managing alliance scope, interfaces and the 'alliance manager' role with cases such as Ford-Mazda and Whirlpool-Philips.
relevance: Theory: the 'extent of organizational interaction' axis is an early operationalisation of integration depth and shows that firms deliberately calibrate it by alliance type. Access: out of print, used copies approx. EUR 10-25.

title: Strategic Alliances: Formation, Implementation, and Evolution
author_source: Lorange and Roos, Blackwell, 1992, monograph
note: Analyses over 30 alliances in the US, Japan and Europe; proposes an archetype typology (ad hoc pool, consortium, project-based JV, full-blown JV) by degree of resource input and retrieval, and a process model of formation, implementation and evolution with nine case histories.
relevance: Theory: the four-archetype model explicitly orders alliances by depth of integration of resources, a direct precursor to differentiated integration in alliances. Access: out of print, used copies approx. EUR 15-40.

title: Cooperative Strategies in International Business: Joint Ventures and Technology Partnerships between Firms
author_source: Contractor and Lorange (eds.), Lexington Books, 1988, edited volume
note: Foundational edited volume of IB alliance research: the editors' framework of the costs and benefits of cooperative arrangements along a continuum from licensing to equity JVs; chapters by Kogut (JV stability), Harrigan, Hennart and others on control, ownership and partner contributions.
relevance: Theory: the 'continuum of cooperative arrangements' is the earliest IB conceptualisation of differentiated depth of integration; historical anchor for the literature review. Access: out of print, used copies approx. EUR 20-40; the Google Books record found appears to be a later reissue, check edition.

title: Strategies for Joint Venture Success
outlet: Praeger, New York (reissued Routledge Library Editions: International Business, 2012)
author_source: Killing, Praeger, 1983, monograph
note: Classic study of 37 JVs that introduced the dominant-parent versus shared-management versus independent JV typology and found dominant-parent ventures easier to manage and better performing; chapters 'Dominant and shared ventures' and 'How to design a shared management joint venture'.
relevance: Theory: the dominant/shared/independent control typology is the earliest empirical treatment of asymmetric partner integration into a venture. Access: free to borrow on Internet Archive; Routledge reissue approx. GBP 30.

title: On the Future of International Joint Venture Research
author_source: Nippa and Reuer, Journal of International Business Studies 50(4), 555-597, 2019, article
note: Comprehensive review of IJV research across formation motives, partner selection, governance and control, management, performance and termination. Diagnoses stagnation in some streams and sets a research agenda including IJV governance as a bundle of mechanisms, dynamics after formation, and multi-partner and emerging-market ventures.
relevance: Review and gap: the agenda explicitly calls for studying IJV governance as a configuration of multiple mechanisms and the evolution of control after formation, which is where differentiated integration across functions and partners fits; prime source for positioning a JIBS-style contribution. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Airline Partnerships, Antitrust Immunity, and Joint Ventures: What We Know and What I Think We Would Like to Know
author_source: Bilotkach, Review of Industrial Organization 54(1), 37-60, 2019, article
note: Survey of empirical research on airline partnerships from code-sharing to immunised joint ventures; summarises price, output and welfare evidence by cooperation level and lists open questions.
relevance: Context/gap: most recent synthesis of integration tiers in airline alliances; DOI from memory, check; WU licence.

title: Differentiated Integration and Disintegration in the EU after Brexit: Risks versus Opportunities
outlet: JCMS: Journal of Common Market Studies
author_source: Leruth, Gänzle and Trondal, JCMS 57(6), 1383-1394, 2019, article
note: Draws on five empirical models of differentiation inside and outside the EU (EEA model, Danish quasi-permanent opt-outs, Swedish de facto differentiation, instrumental model, Brexit as differentiated disintegration) and weighs the risks (fragmentation, legitimacy) and opportunities (flexibility, keeping reluctant members in) of each.
relevance: Theory: introduces differentiated disintegration, the partial exit of a member while remaining tied through selective arrangements, which parallels partial alliance exit, scope reduction and renegotiation in IJVs; the five models give a menu of asymmetric membership forms. Open access.

title: Knowledge Sharing and Safeguarding in R&D Collaborations: The Role of Steering Committees in Biotechnology Alliances
author_source: Devarakonda and Reuer, Strategic Management Journal 39(7), 1912-1934, 2018, article
note: Contract data on biotech alliances; steering committees are used when knowledge sharing needs are high, and their composition and authority are calibrated to appropriation risk.
relevance: Theory/method: committee design as a measurable, graded integration mechanism; WU licence.

title: The Double-Edged Effect of Contracts on Alliance Performance
author_source: Schilke and Lumineau, Journal of Management 44(7), 2827-2858, 2018, article
note: Survey of alliances; control provisions raise conflict while coordination provisions reduce it, so the two contract dimensions have opposite performance effects, moderated by partner differences.
relevance: Theory: distinguishes control-based from coordination-based integration, both measurable in contracts; WU licence.

title: Towards a Theory of Ecosystems
author_source: Jacobides, Cennamo and Gawer, Strategic Management Journal 39(8), 2255-2276, 2018, article
note: Defines ecosystems as sets of actors with varying degrees of multilateral, non-generic complementarities that are not fully hierarchically controlled. Distinguishes unique vs. supermodular complementarities and explains why ecosystems sit between markets, alliances and hierarchies, with the orchestrator setting standards and roles for heterogeneous complementors.
relevance: Theory: ecosystems are multi-partner arrangements in which members are integrated to very different degrees (core complementors, certified partners, open-access participants), the business analogue of variable geometry; the complementarity typology explains which partners need tight integration. Open access article.

title: Free-Riding in Multi-Party Alliances: The Role of Perceived Alliance Effectiveness and Peers' Collaboration in a Research Consortium
author_source: Fonti et al., Strategic Management Journal 38(2), 363-383, 2017, article
note: Survey and network data on a research consortium; members' contribution levels diverge, with free-riding reduced by perceived effectiveness and peer collaboration.
relevance: Theory/method: heterogeneous member commitment in multi-partner alliances, network methods; WU licence.

title: The Effect of Code-Sharing Alliances on Airline Profitability
author_source: Zou and Chen, Journal of Air Transport Management 58, 50-57, 2017, article
note: Panel of airlines; code-sharing alliance intensity affects profitability, with effects depending on alliance type and carrier characteristics.
relevance: Context: links a shallow integration mode (code-share) to performance; DOI and pages not confirmed; WU licence.

title: Strategic Alliance Structures: An Organization Design Perspective
author_source: Albers, Wohlgezogen and Zajac, Journal of Management 42(3), 582-614, 2016, article
note: Review that reframes alliance governance as organisation design: alliance structures combine structural dimensions (centralization, specialization, formalization) and process dimensions (coordination, control, incentives) that can be configured independently, moving beyond the equity vs. non-equity dichotomy.
relevance: Theory: provides the multidimensional design vocabulary needed to describe alliances whose parts are integrated to different degrees (some functions centralised and formalised, others decentralised); the natural bridge between EU differentiated integration and alliance structure. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Mechanisms of Hybrid Governance: Administrative Committees in Non-Equity Alliances
author_source: Reuer and Devarakonda, Academy of Management Journal 59(2), 510-533, 2016, article
note: Biotech-pharma contractual alliances; firms add steering and administrative committees as hierarchical elements when coordination needs and appropriation hazards are high, creating graded integration inside non-equity alliances.
relevance: Theory/data: hand-coded contracts show integration depth varies within a governance form; WU licence.

title: The Group Dynamics of Interorganizational Relationships: Collaborating with Multiple Partners in Innovation Ecosystems
author_source: Davis, Administrative Science Quarterly 61(4), 621-661, 2016, article
note: Inductive multi-case study of computing-industry triads; shows how firms sequence and differentiate collaboration across partners (shared, parallel and dyadic configurations) to manage group dynamics.
relevance: Theory: differentiated engagement across partners within one collaborative group; WU licence.

title: Explaining Differentiation in European Union Treaties
author_source: Winzen and Schimmelfennig, European Union Politics 17(4), 616-637, 2016, article
note: Quantitative test using the EUDIFF dataset of differentiations in EU treaty law 1952-2010 (country-policy-year observations). Finds that differentiation is driven by national identity-based Euroscepticism and by wealth differences (fiscal/transfer concerns), with treaty revisions and enlargements as the occasions; differentiation is a mechanism to let integration proceed despite heterogeneous preferences.
relevance: Method and theory: shows how to build a partner-by-policy-by-year panel of 'who is in which part of the integration' and model it with heterogeneity of preferences and capabilities, directly transferable to multi-partner alliance data (partner x activity x year). Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Good Governance and Differentiated Integration: Graded Membership in the European Union
author_source: Schimmelfennig, European Journal of Political Research 55(4), 789-810, 2016, article
note: Analyses organisational differentiation: states refuse or are refused full membership but settle for in-between grades (EEA, association, neighbourhood). The position of a country in the graded-membership system is explained by its governance quality relative to the core and by its own preferences; integration is a continuum rather than in/out.
relevance: Theory: 'graded membership' is the closest EU analogue to tiered partner status in alliance networks, platform partner programmes and consortia (core partner, associate, affiliate); the good-governance screening logic parallels partner selection on capability and reliability. Paywalled; SSOAR open copy exists.

title: A 22 Year Review of Strategic Alliance Research in the Leading Management Journals
author_source: Gomes, Barnes and Mahmood, International Business Review 25(1), 15-27, 2016, article
note: Reviews strategic alliance articles published 1991-2012 in leading management and IB journals, organised along the alliance life cycle (formation, partner selection, governance and control, implementation and management, performance) and by theoretical lens; documents the dominance of transaction cost, RBV and social exchange perspectives.
relevance: Review: a life-cycle map of alliance research that shows integration decisions studied mostly as a single governance choice at formation, leaving the differentiation of integration across activities and partners over time as a gap. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: The European Union as a System of Differentiated Integration: Interdependence, Politicization and Differentiation
author_source: Schimmelfennig, Leuffen and Rittberger, Journal of European Public Policy 22(6), 764-782, 2015, article
note: Conceptual core of the differentiated-integration (DI) literature. Defines the EU as a system in which integration varies vertically (level of centralisation per policy area) and horizontally (territorial extension, internal and external differentiation). Explains the pattern with interdependence (demand for integration) and politicization (resistance to supranational centralisation): high interdependence plus low politicization yields uniform deep integration, high politicization yields opt-outs and multi-speed arrangements. Lead article of the JEPP special issue on DI.
relevance: Theory: supplies the two-dimensional vertical/horizontal differentiation vocabulary that can be transferred to alliances (depth of integration per activity vs. which partners participate); the interdependence-politicization explanation maps onto partner interdependence and sovereignty/control concerns in IJVs. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: The External Face of Differentiated Integration: Third Country Participation in EU Sectoral Bodies
author_source: Lavenex, Journal of European Public Policy 22(6), 836-853, 2015, article
note: Studies external differentiated integration: non-member states' selective participation in EU agencies, regulatory networks and sectoral bodies. Participation varies by sector and by the functional interdependence and institutional compatibility of the third country; integration without membership is sector-specific and asymmetric.
relevance: Context and theory: shows how outsiders integrate selectively into specific functions of an integrated system, the analogue of non-equity partners or peripheral firms participating in only some activities of an alliance network. Open copy in the UNIGE archive; otherwise WU licence.

title: Board Involvement in International Joint Ventures
author_source: Reuer et al., Strategic Management Journal 35(11), 1626-1644, 2014, article
note: Dutch IJV survey; board involvement in IJV strategy and monitoring increases with asset specificity, environmental uncertainty and partner size asymmetry.
relevance: Theory: explains variation in the depth of governance-level integration across IJVs; WU licence.

title: Divisive Faultlines and the Unplanned Dissolutions of Multipartner Alliances
author_source: Heidl et al., Organization Science 25(5), 1351-1371, 2014, article
note: Multipartner R&D alliances; subgroup faultlines (prior ties, nationality) raise dissolution risk, moderated by alliance size and scope.
relevance: Theory: sub-coalitions inside multi-partner alliances as an endogenous form of variable geometry; WU licence.

title: Instrumental and Constitutional Differentiation in the European Union
outlet: JCMS: Journal of Common Market Studies
author_source: Schimmelfennig and Winzen, JCMS 52(2), 354-370, 2014, article
note: Introduces a new dataset on differentiation in EU treaty law and distinguishes two logics: instrumental differentiation (temporary, originates in enlargement, driven by efficiency and distributional concerns, e.g. transition periods for new members) and constitutional differentiation (long-lasting, originates in treaty revisions, driven by sovereignty concerns, e.g. opt-outs).
relevance: Theory: the instrumental vs. constitutional distinction maps onto transitional, capability-driven asymmetries in alliance integration (new partner phasing in) versus durable, control-driven asymmetries (partner refuses to pool a function); offers a duration-based coding of differentiation. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: A Review of Antecedents of International Strategic Alliance Performance: Synthesized Evidence and New Directions for Core Constructs
author_source: Christoffersen, International Journal of Management Reviews 15(1), 66-85, 2013, article
note: Reviews 165 empirical studies of international strategic alliance performance, synthesising evidence on partner characteristics, cultural distance, trust, commitment, control and governance; finds inconsistent effects for many antecedents and recommends clearer construct definitions and multilevel designs.
relevance: Review: maps the antecedents whose effects on IJV performance are mixed, which a differentiated-integration lens (how much, with whom, in which activity) may reconcile; identifies construct-definition gaps. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Performance Implications of IJV Boards: A Contingency Perspective
authors: Van den Bosch, Frans A. J.
author_source: Klijn et al., Journal of Management Studies 50(7), 1245-1266, 2013, article
note: Dutch IJVs; board involvement in monitoring and advising improves performance only under specific conditions (e.g. partner contributions, uncertainty), so board-based integration is a contingent choice.
relevance: Theory/data: boards as an integration lever beyond equity share; WU licence.

title: Do Regions Matter? An Integrated Institutional and Semiglobalization Perspective on the Internationalization of MNEs
author_source: Arregle, Miller, Hitt and Beamish, Strategic Management Journal 34(8), 910-934, 2013, article
note: Multilevel (country within region within firm) analysis of Japanese MNEs' foreign subsidiaries showing that internationalisation decisions are shaped by regional-level institutional factors and by the firm's existing regional presence; regions are a distinct level of analysis between country and global.
relevance: Method and context: demonstrates three-level hierarchical modelling of firm decisions nested in countries and regions, which can be adapted to alliances nested in partner-dyads and regions when studying regionally differentiated integration. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Coordinating and Competing in Ecosystems: How Organizational Forms Shape New Technology Investments
author_source: Kapoor and Lee, Strategic Management Journal 34(3), 274-296, 2013, article
note: Studies US hospitals' adoption of new medical technologies and shows that the organisational form used to coordinate with complementors (arm's length, alliance, or integration/ownership) shapes investment: alliances with complementors speed adoption more than either arm's-length relations or full integration.
relevance: Theory and evidence: focal firms simultaneously use different coordination forms with different complementors in one ecosystem, i.e. differentiated integration across partners, and the chosen degree of integration affects innovation outcomes. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: The Two Facets of Collaboration: Cooperation and Coordination in Strategic Alliances
author_source: Gulati et al., Academy of Management Annals 6(1), 531-583, 2012, article
note: Review separating cooperation (alignment of interests) from coordination (alignment of actions) and the mechanisms for each; argues most alliance research conflates them.
relevance: Theory: coordination mechanisms as the operational content of integration depth; organising frame for the literature review; WU licence.

title: Network Resource Stocks and Flows: How Do Alliance Portfolios Affect the Value of New Alliance Formations?
author_source: Wassmer and Dussauge, Strategic Management Journal 33(7), 871-883, 2012, article
note: Event study of global airline alliance announcements; the value of a new alliance depends on complementarity and substitutability with resources already accessed through the existing portfolio.
relevance: Data/context: airline alliance data and event-study method; WU licence.

title: Differentiated Integration in the European Union: Many Concepts, Sparse Theory, Few Data
author_source: Holzinger and Schimmelfennig, Journal of European Public Policy 19(2), 292-305, 2012, article
note: Research-agenda piece: reviews the proliferation of DI concepts (multi-speed, variable geometry, a la carte, concentric circles, opt-outs, enhanced cooperation), notes the absence of a general theory and of systematic data, and proposes a measurement scheme (incongruence of membership and rule validity across policy areas and time) plus candidate explanations from club theory, public-goods theory and intergovernmentalism.
relevance: Theory and measurement: the conceptual taxonomy and the proposed indicators (which members are bound by which rules, for how long) offer a template for coding differentiated integration across partners and activities in multi-partner alliances; also diagnoses a sparse-theory, few-data gap that the alliance literature can fill. Paywalled; WU licence; KOPS Konstanz repository copy exists.

title: Antitrust Immunity for Airline Alliances
author_source: Bilotkach and Hüschelrath, Journal of Competition Law & Economics 7(2), 335-380, 2011, article
note: Reviews the economics and policy of antitrust-immunised airline alliances and metal-neutral joint ventures, the deepest integration tier within global alliances.
relevance: Context: defines the immunised-JV tier inside Star/oneworld/SkyTeam; DOI corrected after link check; WU licence.

title: Building Better Causal Theories: A Fuzzy Set Approach to Typologies in Organization Research
author_source: Fiss, Academy of Management Journal 54(2), 393-420, 2011, article
note: Introduces fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) for organisational typologies, distinguishing core from peripheral conditions and showing equifinal configurations of structure, strategy and environment associated with high performance (Miles and Snow typology re-analysed).
relevance: Method: QCA suits the question of which configurations of partner-, activity- and region-specific integration lead to alliance success when the number of alliances is modest and causality is conjunctural; the core/peripheral distinction echoes core vs. peripheral partners. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Alliance Portfolios: A Review and Research Agenda
author_source: Wassmer, Journal of Management 36(1), 141-171, 2010, article
note: Systematic review of alliance-portfolio research organised around portfolio emergence, configuration (size, diversity, tie strength, governance mix) and management, and their effects on firm outcomes; sets out a research agenda on portfolio configuration and inter-alliance interdependencies.
relevance: Review and theory: the portfolio-configuration literature is where heterogeneity of integration across a firm's partners is already measured (governance mix, tie strength, partner diversity); it gives constructs and a gap list for a differentiated-integration study. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Integration on Performance: A Contingency and Configuration Approach
author_source: Flynn, Huo and Zhao, Journal of Operations Management 28(1), 58-71, 2010, article
note: Survey of 617 Chinese manufacturers distinguishing internal, customer and supplier integration. Contingency (regression) and configuration (cluster) analyses show that internal and customer integration matter most for operational and business performance and that balanced high-integration configurations outperform unbalanced ones.
relevance: Method and theory: the contingency-versus-configuration design directly addresses whether uneven (differentiated) integration across partner types helps or hurts, and offers validated multi-item integration scales reusable in alliance surveys. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Parent Contribution and Organizational Control in International Joint Ventures
author_source: Chen et al., Strategic Management Journal 30(11), 1133-1156, 2009, article
note: IJVs in China; parents' relative contributions of tangible and intangible resources predict who controls which organisational dimension (e.g. staffing, operations), and control-contribution fit predicts performance.
relevance: Theory/evidence: resource contribution as the driver of activity-specific control allocation; WU licence.

title: Beyond Entry Mode Choice: Explaining the Conversion of Joint Ventures into Wholly Owned Subsidiaries in the PRC
author_source: Puck et al., Journal of International Business Studies 40(3), 388-404, 2009, article
note: Survey of foreign firms in China; experience, declining need for local knowledge and institutional change explain the move from JV to wholly owned subsidiary, i.e. the deepening of integration after entry.
relevance: Dynamics: integration depth is not fixed at formation; WU (Vienna) authors, useful network; WU licence.

title: Meta-analyses of International Joint Venture Performance Determinants: Evidence for Theory, Methodological Artifacts and the Unique Context of China
author_source: Reus and Rottig, Management International Review 49(5), 607-640, 2009, article
note: Meta-analysis of IJV performance determinants including control, equity share, trust, cultural distance; effects of control and trust are positive but heterogeneous across contexts and measurement artefacts.
relevance: Evidence base: effect sizes for control-performance and trust-performance links; the requested Lee/Yang/Lee meta-analysis could not be located under that name, this is the closest substitute; WU licence.

title: Choice and Performance of Governance Mechanisms: Matching Alliance Governance to Asset Type
author_source: Hoetker and Mellewigt, Strategic Management Journal 30(10), 1025-1044, 2009, article
note: German telecom alliances; formal mechanisms fit property-based assets, relational mechanisms fit knowledge-based assets; mismatch lowers performance.
relevance: Theory: governance mechanisms should differ by the type of activity integrated, a within-alliance differentiation argument; WU licence.

title: The Nature of Partnering Experience and the Gains from Alliances
author_source: Gulati et al., Strategic Management Journal 30(11), 1213-1233, 2009, article
note: Event study of alliance announcements; partner-specific experience raises gains more than general experience, and the benefit depends on alliance type and governance.
relevance: Theory: repeated partner-specific ties as a reason to integrate some partners more deeply than others; WU licence.

title: Marketing Alliances, Firm Networks, and Firm Value Creation
author_source: Swaminathan and Moorman, Journal of Marketing 73(5), 52-69, 2009, article
note: Event study of marketing alliance announcements in the software industry: the firm's alliance network (network efficiency, density, reputation, centrality) shapes the abnormal returns from a new marketing alliance, with marketing alliance capability as mediator; network position moderates value creation.
relevance: Method and theory: combines event-study returns with network measures of the firm's existing portfolio to show that the value of a new partnership depends on how it is embedded in heterogeneous existing ties; supports portfolio-level analysis of differentiated integration. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Friends, Acquaintances, or Strangers? Partner Selection in R&D Alliances
author_source: Li et al., Academy of Management Journal 51(2), 315-334, 2008, article
note: R&D alliances from SDC; firms choose friends over strangers when alliance scope is broad or governance is equity-based, i.e. scope, governance and partner familiarity are traded off.
relevance: Theory/data: links alliance scope and governance form to partner type; shows SDC Platinum can measure scope; WU licence.

title: Alliance Portfolio Internationalization and Firm Performance
author_source: Lavie and Miller, Organization Science 19(4), 623-646, 2008, article
note: US software firms; the internationalization of a firm's alliance portfolio has a sigmoid relationship with performance as coordination and liability-of-foreignness costs rise with partner-country distance.
relevance: Theory/method: the IB bridge between portfolio research and cross-border integration costs; WU licence.

title: Strategic Alliance Contracts: Dimensions and Determinants of Contractual Complexity
author_source: Reuer and Ariño, Strategic Management Journal 28(3), 313-330, 2007, article
note: Spanish alliance survey; contractual complexity has two dimensions, enforcement and coordination provisions, driven by asset specificity and whether duration is pre-specified.
relevance: Method: validated measure of contractual integration depth usable in dyad-level studies; WU licence.

title: Strategies for Managing a Portfolio of Alliances
author_source: Hoffmann, Strategic Management Journal 28(8), 827-856, 2007, article
note: Multiple-case study of Austrian/German firms; distinguishes shaping, adapting and stabilising portfolio strategies and shows firms configure ties of different depth deliberately.
relevance: Theory: portfolio-level differentiation of ties; WU (Vienna) author; DOI from memory, check; WU licence.

title: Alliance Portfolios and Firm Performance: A Study of Value Creation and Appropriation in the U.S. Software Industry
author_source: Lavie, Strategic Management Journal 28(12), 1187-1212, 2007, article
note: Panel of 367 software firms and 20,779 alliances; network resources create value depending on complementarity, while partners' bargaining power and competition in the portfolio shape appropriation.
relevance: Method/data: panel design and SDC-based portfolio measures for a quantitative study; WU licence.
abstract: This study reveals the multifaceted contribution of alliance portfolios to firms' market performance. Extending prior research that has stressed the value-creation effect of network resources, it uncovers how prominent partners may undermine a firm's capacity to appropriate value from its alliance portfolio. Analysis of a comprehensive panel dataset of 367 software firms and their 20,779 alliances suggests that the contribution of network resources to value creation varies with the complementarity of those resources. Furthermore, the relative bargaining power of partners in the alliance portfolio constrains the firm's appropriation capacity, especially when many of these partners compete in the focal firm's industry. In turn, the firm's market performance improves with the intensity of competition among partners in its alliance portfolio.

title: The Performance Implications of Timing of Entry and Involvement in Multipartner Alliances
author_source: Lavie et al., Academy of Management Journal 50(3), 578-604, 2007, article
note: Members of the Wi-Fi Alliance; early entrants and more involved (board-level) members gain more, but involvement effects are contingent on timing, so members at different tiers extract different value.
relevance: Theory/data: multi-partner alliance with graded membership, directly parallel to airline-alliance tiers; WU licence.

title: The Impact of Membership in Competing Alliance Constellations: Evidence on the Operational Performance of Global Airlines
author_source: Lazzarini, Strategic Management Journal 28(4), 345-367, 2007, article
note: Panel of global airlines; constellation membership raises traffic but the benefit depends on the constellation's size and on the member's own bilateral ties, so members gain unevenly.
relevance: Data/method: the standard quantitative airline-constellation study (panel, hand-collected alliance data); WU licence.

title: Building Theoretical and Empirical Bridges Across Levels: Multilevel Research in Management
author_source: Hitt, Beamish, Jackson and Mathieu, Academy of Management Journal 50(6), 1385-1399, 2007, article
note: Editors' essay on multilevel research: reviews bottom-up and top-down cross-level theorising, sampling and measurement issues, and analytic approaches (HLM, cross-level moderation), with illustrations including international joint ventures nested in parents and countries.
relevance: Method: the standard entry point for modelling alliances or partner dyads nested in portfolios, firms and countries, which is required to study integration that varies at partner, activity and region level simultaneously. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Multilateral Airline Alliances: Balancing Strategic Constraints and Opportunities
author_source: Gudmundsson and Lechner, Journal of Air Transport Management 12(3), 153-158, 2006, article
note: Conceptual; multilateral airline alliances constrain members' bilateral partnering while offering network benefits; member heterogeneity and governance explain divergent commitment.
relevance: Context: constellation governance with tiered members; DOI from memory, check; WU licence.

title: Split Management Control and International Joint Venture Performance
author_source: Choi and Beamish, Journal of International Business Studies 35(3), 201-215, 2004, article
note: Korean IJV sample; four control configurations (split, shared, MNE-dominant, local-dominant); split control, where each parent controls the activities matching its firm-specific advantages, outperforms the others.
relevance: Theory/evidence: the clearest empirical case that activity-wise differentiated control (not uniform integration) pays off; DOI taken from search-result URL, check against 8400076; WU licence.

title: The Scope and Governance of International R&D Alliances
author_source: Oxley and Sampson, Strategic Management Journal 25(8-9), 723-749, 2004, article
note: Argues that firms manage knowledge-leakage hazards in international R&D alliances not only through governance (equity vs. contract) but through alliance scope: when partners are direct competitors, firms narrow the scope of the alliance (exclude manufacturing and marketing) rather than adopt more hierarchical governance. Empirical analysis of telecom and electronics alliances.
relevance: Theory: the closest alliance-side analogue to a la carte integration; scope restriction means partners integrate R&D but deliberately keep downstream activities separate, i.e. differentiated integration by activity as a substitute for governance; central reference for the research question. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: A Perspective on Regional and Global Strategies of Multinational Enterprises
author_source: Rugman and Verbeke, Journal of International Business Studies 35(1), 3-18, 2004, article
note: Using sales distribution of the Fortune Global 500, shows that most large MNEs are home-region oriented rather than global; only nine firms qualify as truly global. Argues that firm-specific advantages are often region-bound, so MNEs integrate operations at the regional rather than global level.
relevance: Context and theory: regional strategy is differentiated integration at the firm level (deep integration within the home region, shallow outside) and suggests that cross-border alliances will also be integrated to different degrees by region of the partner. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Semiglobalization and International Business Strategy
author_source: Ghemawat, Journal of International Business Studies 34(2), 138-152, 2003, article
note: Reviews evidence on cross-border integration of product, capital, labour and knowledge markets and concludes that integration is substantial but incomplete (semiglobalization). Argues that incomplete integration is what makes international business strategy distinctive and that location-specificity must be built into strategy models.
relevance: Theory and context: provides the IB counterpart to partial integration: markets and firms integrate to intermediate and varying degrees, so alliances that integrate some activities or regions fully and others not at all are the expected rather than deviant case. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Correcting for Endogeneity in Strategic Management Research
author_source: Hamilton and Nickerson, Strategic Organization 1(1), 51-78, 2003, article
note: Explains why strategy choices (such as governance form) are endogenous to unobserved firm characteristics, reviews switching regressions, Heckman-type selection corrections and instrumental variables, and shows with examples how uncorrected estimates of the performance effect of a strategic choice are biased.
relevance: Method: the degree of integration chosen for each partner or activity is a self-selected choice, so any performance test of differentiated integration needs the selection-correction toolkit this article lays out. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Do Formal Contracts and Relational Governance Function as Substitutes or Complements?
author_source: Poppo and Zenger, Strategic Management Journal 23(8), 707-725, 2002, article
note: Classic; survey of IS outsourcing relationships shows contract customisation and relational governance are complements, each raising the other's performance effect.
relevance: Theory: formal and relational integration as layered, complementary depth dimensions; standard citation; WU licence.

title: Post-Formation Dynamics in Strategic Alliances
author_source: Reuer et al., Strategic Management Journal 23(2), 135-151, 2002, article
note: Biotech-pharma alliances; alliance governance changes after formation (contract alterations, board/committee changes, monitoring changes) are explained by partner experience and the initial governance choice.
relevance: Dynamics/data: shows post-formation changes in integration depth are measurable from alliance records; WU licence.

title: Alliance Constellations: A Social Exchange Perspective
author_source: Das and Teng, Academy of Management Review 27(3), 445-456, 2002, article
note: Conceptual; alliance constellations (multi-firm groupings such as airline alliances) differ from dyadic alliances in size, membership heterogeneity and governance, which social exchange theory explains.
relevance: Theory: constellation-level unit of analysis where member tiers and heterogeneous commitment arise; WU licence.

title: A Dual Parent Perspective on Control and Performance in International Joint Ventures: Lessons from a Developing Economy
author_source: Luo et al., Journal of International Business Studies 32(1), 41-58, 2001, article
note: Matched data from both parents of Sino-foreign IJVs; overall and specific control have different performance effects for the foreign and the local parent, so the same control arrangement is evaluated differently by each side.
relevance: Method/data: dyadic (both-parent) design, a template for alliance-level data on asymmetric integration; WU licence.

title: Trust, Control, and Risk in Strategic Alliances: An Integrated Framework
author_source: Das and Teng, Organization Studies 22(2), 251-283, 2001, article
note: Classic conceptual framework linking goodwill and competence trust, behaviour, output and social control, and relational and performance risk; control mechanisms are chosen per risk type, not uniformly.
relevance: Theory: control-trust lens for why partners accept different control intensities across activities; still the standard citation; WU licence.

title: Levels of Airline Alliance Membership: Balancing Risks and Benefits
author_source: Kleymann and Seristö, Journal of Air Transport Management 7(5), 303-310, 2001, article
note: Conceptual; relates the tightness of a carrier's integration into an alliance group (from code-share to equity) to the risk it bears, and argues that airlines deliberately choose graded membership levels.
relevance: Context: the explicit airline-industry statement of membership tiers as differentiated integration; WU licence.

title: Bringing Together or Driving Apart the Union? Towards a Theory of Differentiated Integration
outlet: Preprints of the Max Planck Institute for Research on Collective Goods, Bonn, 2001/5
author_source: Kölliker, Max Planck Institute for Research on Collective Goods Preprint 2001/5, 2001, working paper (published in West European Politics 24(4), 2001)
note: Develops a public-goods theory of differentiated integration: the centripetal effect of closer cooperation among willing members on initially unwilling outsiders depends on the type of good produced; eventual participation of laggards is most likely for excludable network goods (EMU, Schengen) and least likely for common-pool-resource problems (tax harmonisation).
relevance: Theory: the excludability and rivalry of the benefits an alliance produces predict whether partners who stay outside a sub-group later join (convergence) or whether differentiation becomes permanent; directly transferable to tiered membership in multi-partner alliances and consortia. Paywalled; working-paper version free on EconStor and SSRN.
publisher: Max Planck Institute for Research on Collective Goods

title: The Rational Design of International Institutions
author_source: Koremenos, Lipson and Snidal, International Organization 55(4), 761-799, 2001, article
note: Framework article of the Rational Design project: explains variation in five design dimensions of international institutions (membership, scope, centralization, control, flexibility) by cooperation problems (distribution, enforcement, number of actors, uncertainty about behaviour, state of the world and preferences). Sixteen conjectures, e.g. restrictive membership increases with enforcement problems, flexibility increases with uncertainty.
relevance: Theory: the membership/scope/centralization/control/flexibility dimensions are a ready-made design space for differentiated integration in alliances, and the conjectures (restrictive membership and limited scope under enforcement and distribution problems) can be reformulated as hypotheses on alliance tiers and scope. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: The Optimal Design of International Trade Institutions: Uncertainty and Escape
author_source: Rosendorff and Milner, International Organization 55(4), 829-857, 2001, article
note: Formal model of repeated trade cooperation with domestic political uncertainty: an escape clause that lets a member temporarily deviate at a pre-negotiated cost makes the cooperative regime more durable than a rigid agreement; the optimal cost of escape is positive but finite.
relevance: Theory: escape clauses and temporary opt-outs are a form of differentiated commitment; the model gives a rationale for alliance contracts that let partners suspend participation in some activities without terminating the whole relationship, and predicts when such flexibility stabilises rather than erodes cooperation. Paywalled; SSRN preprint free.

title: The Acquisition and Utilization of Information in New Product Alliances: A Strength-of-Ties Perspective
author_source: Rindfleisch and Moorman, Journal of Marketing 65(2), 1-18, 2001, article
note: Survey of firms in new product alliances: relational embeddedness (strong ties) increases information acquisition and utilisation, and horizontal alliances (with competitors) involve weaker ties but more redundant knowledge than vertical alliances with customers and suppliers; knowledge redundancy and tie strength trade off.
relevance: Theory and measurement: operationalises tie strength and alliance type as dimensions along which the depth of integration with a partner differs, with consequences for learning; a marketing-side template for measuring differentiated integration across partner types. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Arcs of Integration: An International Study of Supply Chain Strategies
author_source: Frohlich and Westbrook, Journal of Operations Management 19(2), 185-200, 2001, article
note: International survey of 322 manufacturers: identifies five 'arcs of integration' (inward-facing, periphery-facing, supplier-facing, customer-facing, outward-facing) that describe how far and in which direction firms integrate with suppliers and customers; the widest arcs show the strongest performance improvements.
relevance: Theory and measurement: the arc metaphor is itself a measure of differentiated integration (direction and breadth of integration with different partner types) and the cluster-analytic approach is directly reusable for classifying alliance integration profiles. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Collaboration Networks, Structural Holes, and Innovation: A Longitudinal Study
author_source: Ahuja, Administrative Science Quarterly 45(3), 425-455, 2000, article
note: Panel study of the international chemicals industry: direct ties, indirect ties and structural holes have distinct effects on patent output; direct ties and indirect ties increase innovation while structural holes reduce it in a collaborative (rather than competitive) setting.
relevance: Theory and method: distinguishes qualitatively different ties within one alliance network and estimates their separate effects with firm-year panel count models; a template for measuring heterogeneous integration across a firm's partners. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Learning from Failure: Towards an Evolutionary Model of Collaborative Ventures
author_source: Ariño and de la Torre, Organization Science 9(3), 306-325, 1998, article
note: Longitudinal case of a failed international JV; shows how perceived inequity triggers renegotiation of commitments and scope, with relational quality mediating the adjustment.
relevance: Dynamics: process model of how integration depth is renegotiated; standard citation; WU licence.

title: Managing the Evolution of Multilateralism
author_source: Downs, Rocke and Barsoom, International Organization 52(2), 397-419, 1998, article
note: Explains the breadth-depth trade-off in multilateral cooperation and shows that admitting members sequentially, starting with those with the strongest preference for deep cooperation, creates a structure-induced equilibrium that preserves depth while expanding membership. Evidence from the history of EU enlargement and twenty environmental multilaterals.
relevance: Theory: the sequential-club logic (deep core first, later entrants accept the acquis) is a model for multi-partner alliances and consortia that start with a tightly integrated core and add peripheral partners under differentiated terms; links directly to the breadth-depth trade-off in alliance portfolios. Paywalled; WU licence. DOI from memory, verify.

title: Alliances and Networks
author_source: Rowley, Behrens and Krackhardt, Strategic Management Journal 21(3), 369-386, 2000, article
note: Tests strong vs. weak ties (relational embeddedness) and dense vs. sparse networks (structural embeddedness) as alternative governance mechanisms in the steel and semiconductor industries; strong ties pay off in exploitation-oriented (steel) and weak ties in exploration-oriented (semiconductor) environments, and dense networks with strong ties are redundant.
relevance: Theory: the one allowed network classic; frames alliance governance and evolution as functions of position in a network of heterogeneous ties, which supports the view that a firm integrates differently with different partners according to embeddedness. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Accounting for Endogeneity When Assessing Strategy Performance: Does Entry Mode Choice Affect FDI Survival?
author_source: Shaver, Management Science 44(4), 571-585, 1998, article
note: Shows with data on foreign entries into the US that the apparent survival advantage of greenfield over acquisition entry disappears once the endogenous choice of entry mode is modelled (two-stage selection model); firms choose the mode that suits them, so naive comparisons are biased.
relevance: Method: the canonical IB demonstration that governance or integration mode is endogenous to performance; essential citation for any design that compares outcomes of alliances or partners integrated to different degrees. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Knowledge, Bargaining Power, and the Instability of International Joint Ventures
author_source: Inkpen and Beamish, Academy of Management Review 22(1), 177-202, 1997, article
note: Classic conceptual paper: as the foreign parent acquires local knowledge its dependence on the local partner falls, shifting bargaining power and making the IJV unstable (renegotiation, buy-out, termination).
relevance: Theory: dynamic explanation for why depth of integration is renegotiated over time, the alliance analogue to multi-speed integration; WU licence.

title: Control and Performance in International Joint Ventures
author_source: Mjoen and Tallman, Organization Science 8(3), 257-274, 1997, article
note: Survey of Norwegian parents of IJVs; distinguishes equity share from specific (activity-level) and overall control; specific control over own-contributed resources, not equity, is what predicts performance.
relevance: Theory/method: separates ownership from activity-specific control, the core distinction for differentiated integration; structural equation modelling of dyadic survey data; WU licence.

title: Appropriability Hazards and Governance in Strategic Alliances: A Transaction Cost Approach
outlet: Journal of Law, Economics, and Organization
author_source: Oxley, Journal of Law, Economics, and Organization 13(2), 387-409, 1997, article
note: Orders alliance governance forms on a continuum from unilateral contracts via bilateral contracts to equity JVs and shows, with ordered-probit models on CATI data for US technology alliances, that greater appropriability hazards (weak IPR protection, technology-intensive and multi-activity alliances) shift governance towards more hierarchical forms.
relevance: Theory and method: treats governance as an ordinal degree of integration and models its determinants with ordered probit, an approach that can be applied to each activity or partner dyad within a multi-partner alliance to measure differentiated integration. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: The Evolution of Cooperation in Strategic Alliances: Initial Conditions or Learning Processes?
author_source: Doz, Strategic Management Journal 17(S1), 55-83, 1996, article
note: Classic longitudinal case study; alliances evolve through cycles of learning, re-evaluation and readjustment of task definition, governance and interface design.
relevance: Dynamics: standard citation for adjusting integration scope over time; WU licence.

title: A Categorization of Differentiated Integration
outlet: JCMS: Journal of Common Market Studies
author_source: Stubb, Journal of Common Market Studies 34(2), 283-295, 1996, article
note: The classic typology of flexible integration along three dimensions: time (multi-speed), space (variable geometry) and matter (a la carte). Sorts the political rhetoric of the pre-1996 IGC debate into these categories and clarifies which forms are temporary versus permanent.
relevance: Theory: the time/space/matter triad is the simplest frame for differentiated integration in alliances (partners joining at different speeds, only some partners in some activities, partners choosing menus of activities). Short, highly citable origin article. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: An Economic Model of International Joint Venture Strategy
author_source: Buckley and Casson, Journal of International Business Studies 27(5), 849-876, 1996, article
note: Internalisation-theory model of the choice between international joint venture, licensing and merger using eight factors (market size, pace of technological change, economies of scope, protection of technology, cultural distance, etc.). Treats the IJV as an intermediate form that internalises some flows between partners while keeping others at arm's length.
relevance: Theory: the model explains which activities partners internalise jointly and which they leave outside the venture, i.e. the degree of integration is chosen activity by activity; a direct internalisation-theory foundation for differentiated integration within IJVs. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: When Competition Eclipses Cooperation: An Event History Analysis of Joint Venture Failure
author_source: Park and Russo, Management Science 42(6), 875-890, 1996, article
note: Event-history (hazard) analysis of joint ventures in the electronics industry: ventures between direct competitors fail sooner, while prior ties between partners and broader venture scope reduce the hazard of dissolution; distinguishes termination by acquisition from termination by liquidation.
relevance: Method and theory: template for survival analysis of alliance termination and partial exit, and evidence that scope and competitive overlap, both dimensions of differentiated integration, shape duration. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: Configurations of Strategy and Structure in Subsidiaries of Multinational Corporations
author_source: Birkinshaw and Morrison, Journal of International Business Studies 26(4), 729-753, 1995, article
note: Survey of subsidiaries; local implementer, specialised contributor and world mandate roles differ systematically in autonomy, integration and control.
relevance: Theory: differentiated subsidiary roles as analogy for differentiated partner roles; WU licence.

title: Bargaining Power, Management Control, and Performance in United States-China Joint Ventures: A Comparative Case Study
author_source: Yan and Gray, Academy of Management Journal 37(6), 1478-1517, 1994, article
note: Classic. Four-case comparative study of US-China JVs; bargaining power (resource contributions, alternatives) determines the pattern of management control, which in turn drives performance; control is partitioned across functions, not held uniformly.
relevance: Theory: bargaining-power explanation for why partners integrate different functions to different degrees; qualitative method useful for theory-building; DOI not re-checked; WU licence.

title: Differentiated Fit and Shared Values: Alternatives for Managing Headquarters-Subsidiary Relations
author_source: Nohria and Ghoshal, Strategic Management Journal 15(6), 491-502, 1994, article
note: Classic; MNEs perform better when the structure of each HQ-subsidiary relation fits that subsidiary's context (differentiated fit) or when shared values substitute for structural control.
relevance: Theory: differentiated fit is the template hypothesis for partner-specific integration in alliances; standard citation; WU licence.

title: Organizing Successful Co-Marketing Alliances
author_source: Bucklin and Sengupta, Journal of Marketing 57(2), 32-46, 1993, article
note: Survey of co-marketing alliances (lateral relationships between firms at the same channel level, e.g. in high-tech products). Power and managerial imbalance between partners reduce alliance effectiveness, while project payoff, organisational compatibility and contractual safeguards increase it; shows how asymmetry between partners is managed.
relevance: Theory and context: marketing-alliance counterpart in which partners contribute and integrate unequally; identifies power imbalance and compatibility as moderators of asymmetric integration and offers survey measures of alliance effectiveness. Paywalled; WU licence. DOI constructed from SAGE pattern, verify.

title: Control and Performance of International Joint Ventures
author_source: Geringer and Hebert, Journal of International Business Studies 20(2), 235-254, 1989, article
note: Classic (still the standard citation). Conceptualises IJV control along three dimensions: focus (which activities are controlled), extent (degree) and mechanisms; argues parents control selectively rather than uniformly and links control configurations to performance.
relevance: Theory: the focus/extent/mechanism triad is the natural operationalisation of 'differentiated' (activity-selective) integration at the IJV level; paywalled, WU licence.

title: Internal Differentiation within Multinational Corporations
author_source: Ghoshal and Nohria, Strategic Management Journal 10(4), 323-337, 1989, article
note: Classic; headquarters-subsidiary relations within one MNE are differentiated (centralisation, formalisation, normative integration) according to subsidiary environment and resources.
relevance: Theory: the MNE-internal origin of 'differentiated' governance that can be transposed to alliance partners; standard citation; WU licence.

title: A Transaction Costs Theory of Equity Joint Ventures
author_source: Hennart, Strategic Management Journal 9(4), 361-374, 1988, article
note: Transaction-cost theory of equity JVs distinguishing scale JVs (parents internalise a failing market but indivisibilities make full ownership inefficient) from link JVs (simultaneous market failure for the services of two firm-specific assets, e.g. technology and local distribution). Equity JVs arise when combining assets through contracts or acquisition is more costly than shared ownership.
relevance: Theory: the scale/link distinction predicts which contributions are pooled in the venture and which stay with the parent, so the degree of integration differs by asset and by partner; a foundation for explaining asymmetric integration in IJVs. Paywalled; WU licence.

title: An Economic Theory of Clubs
author_source: Buchanan, Economica 32(125), 1-14, 1965, article
note: Founding article of club theory: goods between private and pure public goods are shared by an excludable group; derives optimal club size from the trade-off between cost sharing and congestion and states the provision, utilisation and membership conditions.
relevance: Theory: the micro-foundation behind variable geometry and tiered membership (Kölliker, Holzinger and Schimmelfennig rely on it); for alliances it frames why a sub-set of partners may form a deeper inner club for a specific activity and how optimal club size limits the number of fully integrated partners. Paywalled (JSTOR); WU licence.

title: Unlocking Strategic Alliances: The Role of Common Institutional Blockholders in Promoting Collaboration and Trust
author_source: Chemmanur, Shen and Xie, SSRN working paper 4509164, 2023, working paper
note: Finance working paper showing that firms sharing common institutional blockholders are more likely to form strategic alliances, choose deeper governance forms and sustain them, interpreting common ownership as a trust and commitment device that reduces hold-up; uses large-sample alliance data (SDC) with ownership data.
relevance: Method and data: recent large-N evidence on what shifts partners towards deeper integration; the ownership-link mechanism is relevant to equity-linked alliances such as Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi. Access: free on SSRN.

title: Die Bedeutung der weichen Erfolgsfaktoren im Management der chinesisch-deutschen Joint Ventures
author_source: Jiang, Dissertation Universität Osnabrück, 2018, thesis
note: Doctoral thesis on soft success factors (trust, culture, communication, commitment) in the management of Chinese-German joint ventures, with empirical evidence from JV managers; discusses how partners divide and share management functions.
relevance: Context: recent German-language empirical work on IJV management between culturally distant partners; relevant for the partner-level differentiation of roles. Access: open access (university repository).

title: Airline Alliances (lecture manuscript, Institute of Air and Space Law)
outlet: McGill University, Institute of Air and Space Law, manuscript
author_source: Dempsey, McGill Institute of Air and Space Law manuscript, 2017, manuscript
note: Extended manuscript on airline alliances by a leading air-law scholar: history and typology of alliances (interline, code-share, franchise, equity, global alliances, immunised JVs), the economics of alliances, US antitrust immunity and EU competition decisions, and the 2010 EC-DOT transatlantic report.
relevance: Context: detailed institutional typology of alliance integration levels and the regulatory decisions that create tiered membership; useful background for case construction. Access: free PDF.

title: Antitrust Immunity and International Airline Alliances
outlet: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division, Economic Analysis Group Discussion Paper EAG 11-1
publisher: US Department of Justice, Economic Analysis Group
author_source: Gillespie and Richard, US DOJ EAG Discussion Paper 11-1, 2011, working paper
note: DOJ economists' empirical analysis of fares on transatlantic routes comparing immunised alliance partners, non-immunised alliance partners and code-share-only cooperation; finds that alliance cooperation without immunity already achieves most of the fare benefits, questioning the incremental value of antitrust immunity for metal-neutral JVs.
relevance: Method and data: directly compares outcomes across integration tiers within the same alliances, i.e. an empirical test of whether deeper (differentiated) integration pays; author names recorded from recollection of the EAG series and should be checked against the PDF. Access: open access via EconStor.

title: Successfully Managing Alliance Portfolios: An Alliance Capability View
author_source: Saebi, PhD thesis, Maastricht University, 2011, thesis
note: Doctoral thesis on alliance portfolio management from an alliance-capability view: conceptualises portfolio-level capabilities (configuration, coordination, learning), studies how firms balance exploration and exploitation alliances and manage interdependencies among partners, with survey and case evidence.
relevance: Theory and method: portfolio configuration and coordination capabilities explain how a focal firm manages partners integrated to different depths; survey instrument reusable. Access: open access PDF.

title: Airline Alliances, Antitrust Immunity and Market Foreclosure
publisher: ZEW - Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research
author_source: Bilotkach and Hüschelrath, ZEW Discussion Paper 10-083, 2010/2012, working paper (published in Review of Economics and Statistics)
note: Tests whether airline partnerships with antitrust immunity foreclose rivals: airlines outside an immunised partnership reduce traffic to the partners' hub airports by 2.6-8.5 percent, consistent with immunised partners refusing connecting passengers from non-partners. Companion ZEW DP 10-080 'Antitrust Immunity for Airline Alliances' reviews the regulatory economics.
relevance: Method and data: quantitative identification of the effects of the deepest integration tier (immunised JVs) relative to ordinary alliance membership, using DOT T-100/DB1B data; shows that differentiated integration has externalities on non-integrated partners.
